parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Section four. You will hear a psychology lecture on the topic of laughter. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Today I'm going to talk about something I hope you will find amusing because the topic is laughter. Despite its prominence in daily life, there has been little research on laughter. So after I became interested in this subject, I started off by having three of my psychology students conduct an observational survey as a component of the course which was designed to focus on the methodology used in this field. The students and I observed twelve hundred people laughing spontaneously in their day-to-day worlds, from the university library to the city streets. Whenever we heard laughter, we noted down information about the exchange. As to our findings, well, we usually think of laughter coming from an audience after something funny has been said by a single speaker. But contrary to our expectations, the speakers we observed laughed about fifty percent more often than their audiences. Our observations also showed that simple everyday comments like, "Where have you been?" are far more likely to precede laughter than a joke is. In fact, only ten to twenty percent of the laughter episodes we witnessed followed anything actually funny. The gender difference in laughter is also striking. In our twelve hundred case studies, we found that while everyone laughed a lot, females laugh one hundred and twenty-six percent more often than their male counterparts. But men seem to be the main instigators of humor across cultures. I also had students in my classes note down in a diary instances when they themselves laughed. When they analyzed the results, they found that laughter for them was thirty times more frequent in social situations than when they are alone. This suggests that laughter is a signal we send to others. Now, moving on from this research to some more general observations, what do we know about the phenomenon of laughter and its psychological features? Oftentimes, if one person laughs, those around that person will also laugh even if they didn't hear or see what caused the laughter. Consider the extraordinary outbreak of laughter at one boarding school some years ago. The symptoms appeared when three students started laughing and couldn't stop. The symptoms rapidly spread, eventually affecting ninety-five students and forcing the school to close until the laughing stopped. Quite an amazing tale, I think you'll agree. What part of the brain controls laughter? Well, when a speaker laughs, the laugh usually occurs at the end of sentences or phrases rather than being randomly scattered through the sentence. This suggests that different regions of the brain are involved in speech, which is largely based on cognition and laughter, which is based on emotion. The physiological effects of laughter are incompletely documented, and their medical benefits are even less certain. But it is known that in many people laughter does, at least temporarily, raise blood pressure. Results of other studies have proved less definite. At least one study reported that comedy and laughter increased the levels of certain chemicals in the urine that were known to be associated with stress. On the other hand, other research in the US reported that laughter reduced these same chemical levels, which indicated the exact opposite effect. So it is far from certain what the effects of laughter are on these particular chemicals, and thus the ultimate effects of laughter in this regard. However, one of laughter's most promising applications, which has been rather extensively noted experimentally, is the reduction of the extent to which we feel pain. One American university study found that this was tolerated better by subjects who laughed at the films of certain comedians than by other subjects who did not watch the films. In another American study, patients who had undergone surgery and then watched comedy films requested fewer aspirin and tranquilizers than others who had viewed serious dramatic films. And science has long understood that laughter causes the prefrontal cortex of the brain to release a certain hormone which makes the person feel happy, although the exact mechanism is not completely understood, nor is its effect. Is laughter universal among humans?

That is the end of section four. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到，这门课程（course）的设计重点是聚焦于该领域所使用的“methodology”（方法论）。
你可能会听到前面的“survey”，但它是用来修饰调查本身的，题目问的是课程（course）的研究目标，必须填入“methodology”。

So after I became interested in this subject, I started off by having three of my psychology students conduct an observational survey as a component of the course which was designed to focus on the methodology used in this field.
录音提到日常评论（everyday comments）引发笑声的可能性远远大于“joke”（笑话）。
这里是在做对比（more likely to... than...），你不要被前文搞笑的问句“Where have you been?”带偏，要准确抓取than后面的比较对象“joke”。
Our observations also showed that simple everyday comments like, "Where have you been?" are far more likely to precede laughter than a joke is.
录音中明确说明，在性别差异中，“females”（女性）笑的频率比男性高出126%。
紧接着虽然提到了男性（male/men），但那是作为对比的一方或是幽默的发起者，题目问的是更倾向于频繁笑的人，因此只能填“females”。

The gender difference in laughter is also striking. In our twelve hundred case studies, we found that while everyone laughed a lot, females laugh one hundred and twenty-six percent more often than their male counterparts. But men seem to be the main instigators of humor across cultures.
录音指出，教授让学生们在“diary”（日记）中记下自己笑的场合。
题目中的“keep a ...”对应录音里的“note down in a ...”，听到记录的载体即可，注意不要错填成后面的“instances”。
I also had students in my classes note down in a diary instances when they themselves laughed.
录音结尾总结道，在社交场合笑得更多，这表明笑是我们发送给他人的一种“signal”（信号）。
虽然前面提到了“social situations”，但那是具体场景，题目问的是笑的功能（functions as），对应录音中的“is a...”，你需要精准捕捉核心名词“signal”。

When they analyzed the results, they found that laughter for them was thirty times more frequent in social situations than when they are alone. This suggests that laughter is a signal we send to others.
录音明确说到，笑声通常出现在句子或短语的“end”（末尾）。
题干的“happen at”对应录音的“occurs at”，听到这里直接锁定名词“end”，不要被后面补充说明的“scattered”（分散的）干扰。
What part of the brain controls laughter? Well, when a speaker laughs, the laugh usually occurs at the end of sentences or phrases rather than being randomly scattered through the sentence.
录音提到说话主要基于认知（cognition），而笑声（laughter）则基于“emotion”（情感）。
这里极其容易把speech对应的“cognition”错当成答案，你必须听清后面“and laughter”紧接着的补充说明，才能抓准专属笑声的“emotion”。
This suggests that different regions of the brain are involved in speech, which is largely based on cognition and laughter, which is based on emotion.
录音指出，笑会增加某些化学物质的水平，而这些物质已知与“stress”（压力）有关。
题干的“linked with”对应录音里的“associated with”，紧跟其后的词就是答案，注意不要填成前面用来铺垫的名词“chemicals”或“urine”。

Results of other studies have proved less definite. At least one study reported that comedy and laughter increased the levels of certain chemicals in the urine that were known to be associated with stress.
录音提到笑最有前景的应用之一，是减少我们感受到的“pain”（疼痛）程度。
题目里的“reduce the feeling of”对应录音中有点复杂的从句“reduction of the extent to which we feel”，你需要直接抓住核心动作“feel”后的宾语“pain”。
However, one of laughter's most promising applications, which has been rather extensively noted experimentally, is the reduction of the extent to which we feel pain.
录音提到笑会导致大脑前额皮质释放一种“hormone”（荷尔蒙/激素），让人感到快乐。
题目中的“produce a kind of”对应录音里的“release a certain”，不要被后面修饰结果的“happy”或补充说明的“mechanism”带偏，注意词性要求是名词。

And science has long understood that laughter causes the prefrontal cortex of the brain to release a certain hormone which makes the person feel happy, although the exact mechanism is not completely understood, nor is its effect.
